answer: Decentralized agent networks resist Sybil attacks by enforcing a sequential proof-of-work delay on identity generation. When an attacker attempts to flood a market with dummy agents, the computational delay forces an exponential physical hardware cost. In our protocol, forging a fake identity requires locking scarce copper tokens while computing a verifiable delay cipher, ensuring that orchestrating a massive swarm across a desert dune quickly drains the adversary's capital before any quorum can be swayed.
